title: Maximum Product Subarray
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Find the maximum product of a contiguous subarray.
intuition: Unlike sums, a negative number can turn the smallest product into the largest. So carry both the running maximum and the running minimum, and swap them whenever you hit a negative.

approaches.title: Brute: all subarrays
Optimal: dual max/min DP
approaches.idea: On a negative element, swap cur_max and cur_min before extending.
approaches.dryRun:
a=[2,3,-2,4]
x=3: max 6 min 3
x=-2: swap -> max 3 min 6; then max=max(-2,-6)=-2, min=min(-2,-12)=-12
x=4: max=max(4,-8)=4; best stays 6
approaches.whyWorks: The optimal product ending at i is either x alone, max*x, or min*x — three candidates, O(1) state.

approaches.title: Alternative: prefix and suffix products
approaches.idea: Scan both directions resetting on zero; take the best value seen.
approaches.whyWorks: An optimal subarray with an even number of negatives is a prefix or suffix of a zero-free block.

commonMistakes: Reusing Kadane unchanged and losing the negative-times-negative case
Resetting to 0 on a zero rather than to the element itself
patternRecognition: Non-monotone operations -> carry both extremes in the DP state
followUps: Subarray product less than K (sliding window)
interviewInsight: Articulating "negatives flip the ordering, so min is a candidate for max" is the whole solution.
